newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: HK businesses seek Manila entry to ASEAN market.
newsitem.headline: HK businesses seek Manila entry to ASEAN market.

text.p: Hong Kong businessmen are looking at the Philippines as their entry point to the growing ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA), a leader of a Hong Kong investment mission to the Philippines said on Wednesday.

Sidney Fung, assistant director for international affairs at the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce, said Hong Kong businessmen were exploring investment opportunities in Southeast Asia after China tightened its investment regulations for foreign companies.
"They are looking around the region for investment opportunities ... It is getting difficult to invest in China because of many regulations and increased red tape," Fung said.

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) which comprises the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and Brunei, have agreed to form a free trade area by the turn of the century.
Fung said the businessmen were not in the Philippines to investigate possible relocation after the British colony reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 next year.
Many delegates said they were looking to forge possible tie-ups with Philippine businesses.

The 30-member delegation began its four-day mission to the country on Wednesday, meeting local businessmen. They are sheduled to visit the Subic free port area and other special economic zones in northern Philippines.
The delegation includes businessmen with interests in fruit and seafood, banking and finance, brokerage, shipping, plastics, and jewellery.
